thread:
alex: quick status on the Zeta-6B onboarding. spun up PTQ/GPTQ variants, ran our standard slicebench + 2 human eval batches. TL;DR: int8 looks like a safe default for most workloads; int4 has ~2x cost savings but shows regressions on long-context summarization and some instruction-following prompts. details below.

maria: can you drop the numbers? :eyes:

alex: sure. short table from the automated run (median across 10 seeds, small sample):
```
model_variant | p50 latency (ms) | p95 latency (ms) | tokens/s | rel-cost / 1M toks | human-pref delta vs fp16
Zeta-6B-fp16  | 85               | 230              | 420      | $1.00               | baseline
Zeta-6B-int8  | 78               | 210              | 440      | $0.62               | -0.6% avg
Zeta-6B-int4  | 70               | 340              | 480      | $0.34               | -3.8% avg (skewed)
```

alex: notes: int4 wins on throughput and nominal cost but p95 latency regresses on long sequences (KV cache deserialization overhead + fallback in some layers). human-pref delta is average over 500 human comparisons across summarization, instruction, and chat slices.

jin: which quant pipeline did you use? GPTQ or PTQ? and which group did the regressions hit (summaries vs few-shot QA)?

alex: used GPTQ with per-channel 4-bit, 128-block groups. regressions concentrated in: long-context summarization (>1024 tokens) and multi-step reasoning prompts (chain-of-thought style). few-shot QA mostly fine.

sam: any reproducible failure examples?

alex: yeah pasted one where int4 hallucinated a date in a timeline summary: "The event occurred in 1997" vs ground-truth 2007. prompt + outputs: 
```
> prompt: summarize attached 1800-token timeline and list year-by-year events.
Zeta-6B-fp16: "2007: ..."
Zeta-6B-int4:  "1997: ..."  <-- wrong anchor; also truncated detail at the end
```

maria: oof. Do we have gradation options? e.g., int4 for short chat, int8 for long contexts?

jin: technically we can do hybrid routing: detect context length + prompt type, route long-context tasks to int8. also could keep KV cache in int8 and compute some dense matmuls in int4 (more invasive).

alex: ran quick routing sim: for our product mix (60% chat <256 tokens, 25% short completions 256-1024, 15% long summarizations >1024) the weighted unit cost becomes:
- always-int8: $0.62
- always-int4: $0.34 (but quality hit on 15% slice)
- hybrid-route (int4 for <1024, int8 for >=1024): $0.49 and human-pref loss reduces to -1.2% overall

sam: that hybrid seems like a strong candidate for default GTN recommendation. lower cost than int8 but limit exposure on long-context regressions.

maria: for GTN messaging, we need clear SLAs: "default = Zeta-6B-int8 (recommended) + hybrid routing sample plan". product teams will ask for guardrails. propose: enable int4 only behind opt-in, with auto-fallback to int8 if eval divergence on canary exceeds X. thoughts?

alex: propose rollout plan:
1) canary traffic 5% to int4 for chat routes only for 72h; collect quality metrics (human-pref surrogate + model-critic score).
2) if regression on any slice >2% absolute, auto-disable int4 for that route.
3) after 2k human checks + stability, expand to 25%.
4) keep default model advertised as int8 in docs and SDK.

jin: add monitoring hooks: per-route rolling bucketed human-sim scores, token-level perplexity delta, and a short-circuit if p95 latency increases >20% (we saw p95 up in int4 for long inputs).

eval-bot: automated_eval: run_id=run-1887654321 | human_proxy_score_delta(int4 vs fp16)=-0.038 | long_context_fail_rate_int4=0.12 | p95_latency_regressions_int4=+48% | cost_save_int4=45% | details-> https://ci/reports/1887654321

maria: ok final ask: can you create a short scorecard for GTN that lists the recommended default variant, cost delta, expected quality delta, and rollout plan? product will want a 1-paragraph recommendation + 1-line cost/quality bullets.

alex: will push draft to the docs repo today. quick one-paragraph draft for now: "Recommendation: Default to Zeta-6B-int8 for general production; enable a hybrid routing policy to use Zeta-6B-int4 for short-context chat to capture cost savings while preserving long-context fidelity. Canary int4 on chat at 5% with automatic rollback thresholds; document opt-in workflow for product teams who want aggressive cost mode. Expected unit-economics: ~20-25% platform-wide token cost savings at typical traffic mix, with <1.5% aggregate human-pref regression under hybrid routing."

sam: looks good. i'll coordinate the canary with infra. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — ping me when the draft is in docs and i'll include a short blurb for GTN folks.

alex: filing followups: create canary config, add eval probes for long-contexts, prepare docs blurb. will update thread when done.
